alt: Screenshot of Google Earth's AI image creation interface showing a prompt-generated futuristic fantasy city with glowing green hyperloop pathways, a massive transparent dome arena, and a spiraling tower, overlaid on real satellite imagery of a city grid, with 'Refine image' and 'Save to project' buttons visible and a disclaimer reading 'Generative AI can make mistakes, so double-check it'
story: On July 31, 2026, Google launched an AI image generation feature for Google Earth that let users prompt-generate fake imagery and superimpose it over real satellite maps; after critics flagged that this gave anyone a tool to fabricate evidence using 'one of the most reliable sources of visual evidence,' Google pulled the feature the following day — while it was live the disclaimer read 'Generative AI can make mistakes, so double-check it.'
why_funny: Google built a way to put photorealistic fake cities on real maps, released it to the public, and then noticed this was a bad idea at exactly the same moment everyone else did.
